newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government watches Norilsk Nickel events.
newsitem.headline: Russian government watches Norilsk Nickel events.

text.p: The Russian government is closely monitoring events at Norilsk Nickel's main mining and metals plant, where workers have threatened to strike over arrears, cabinet spokesman Igor Shabdurasulov said on Tuesday.
"The situation at Norilsk Nickel is under the close scrutiny of the government," he told a news conference.
He also said the government had not yet decided whether to order direct transfers from the federal budget to help pay for Norilsk's social costs in the Arctic where the plant is located.
"As regards concrete transfers from the federal budget, I am not sure that this is the best solution," he said.
He said there were other shareholders in RAO Norilsky Nickel which could help the company pay off its debts.
Commercial bank Uneximbank controls a 38 percent stake, or 51 percent of voting shares, in the Norilsk group. It acquired the stake in a government shares-for-loans scheme in 1995.
Shabdurasulov said First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin and other officials were looking into the Norilsk problem.
Potanin is the former head of Uneximbank.
The Norilsk Nickel group owes workers around 900 billion ($160 million) in salary and holiday arrears and another 1.2 trillion ($211 million) to various budgets.
It wants to shift some of the burden of social costs in the towns where it operates to regional budgets.
Shabdurasulov said the government had been in talks with regional authorities in the Krasnoyarsk region, which has jurisdiction over Norilsk.
